highlights.title: Unitree IPO: Why Investors Are Betting Big on China’s Humanoid Robots
highlights.description: Robots built to move, work and act like humans. It’s a global industry Morgan Stanley estimates could be worth $5 trillion by 2050. It’s also one of the frontiers in the China-US race for technological supremacy.

highlights.title: Pony AI CEO Peng Optimistic on Growth Outlook
highlights.description: James Peng, CEO of Pony AI, says the company plans to expand its robotaxi fleet across more Chinese cities to meet growing demand. He speaks to David Ingles and Yvonne Man on "Bloomberg: The China Show."  (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: China Lands Rocket Back on Earth in Push to Catch Up With SpaceX
highlights.description: China said it recovered a rocket booster on land for the first time, a major step toward catching up with US firms like Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

highlights.title: Chip Selloff Extends to Asia as Samsung, SK Hynix Slump
highlights.description: A global selloff in semiconductor stocks deepened as investors retreated from one of the year’s hottest trades. Shares of Samsung and SK Hynix slumped more than 7% in Seoul after losses in US chipmakers sent the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 5% on Tuesday. Bloomberg's Winnie Hsu has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Baidu says Chinese buyers want local AI chips due to ‘supply chain’ issues
highlights.description: It seems like Nvidia’s not getting back into the Middle Kingdom anytime soon

highlights.title: LG AI Research's Lee on The Importance of Sovereign AI
highlights.description: LG AI Research Head of Superintelligence Lab Lee Moon Tae shares his perspective on the future of superintelligence, the opportunities it unlocks and the responsibilities that come with building AI for the next era. He speaks with Haslinda Amin from the sidelines of 'AI Summit Seoul & Expo 2026'. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Rebellions CFO: Preparing for IPO in Korea
highlights.description: Sungkyue Shin, CFO of AI chip startup Rebellions, says the company is in active preparations for an IPO, with a listing on South Korea's main stock exchange as its top priority. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Paul Allen from the sidelines of the AI Summit & Expo in Seoul. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.description: Cerebras Systems Inc. introduced a new speedier computer built with the company’s chips, saying the device will give it a wider advantage over Nvidia Corp. equipment.

highlights.title: GLM-5.3 hits the API at $1.4/$4.4 per million tokens
highlights.description:
After a stunning debut last week with cyber capabilities so advanced they reportedly found a previously undetected vulnerability in Cursor, GLM-5.3, the new frontier open source language model from Chinese startup z.ai, has now hit the application programming interface (API) — allowing developers the ability to build atop it and plug it into their agents and applications. 
Developers who previously subscribed to a GLM Coding Plan are currently limited to the OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible protocol. Z.ai said it plans to make the model's weights openly available, but a precise date and licensing remain to be seen. 
On the API, the price is unchanged from GLM-5.2: $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens. Cached input costs $0.26 per million tokens, while Z.ai currently lists cached-input storage as free for a limited time. 
That means developers can move to the new generation without taking a higher posted per-token rate from Z.ai, even as the company claims substantially stronger coding and long-horizon agent performance.
At those rates, GLM-5.3 sits well below several of the highest-end frontier APIs.

Using the simple VentureBeat comparison of one million input tokens plus one million output tokens, GLM-5.3 comes to $5.80, versus $8 for Grok 4.6 at its lower context rate, $18 for Kimi K3, $30 for Claude Opus 5 and $35 for GPT-5.6 Sol. 
That is not a workload-cost estimate — real bills depend heavily on the input/output mix, caching and token consumption — but it makes the relative API price tier easy to see.
GLM-5.3 is not the cheapest capable model available. Google’s current introductory price for Gemini 3.7 Flash is $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through Dec. 31, 2026, while OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Luna is priced at $0.20 input and $1.20 output. 
Still, Z.ai’s price puts GLM-5.3 into a notably lower cost band than the premium frontier models it is increasingly benchmarked against.
That comparison has become more relevant following the latest independent results. Artificial Analysis gives GLM-5.3 a score of 60 on its Intelligence Index, tying Kimi K3 as the top performing open weights model in the world, and scoring seven points higher than GLM-5.2. I
ts analysis also estimates GLM-5.3 at about $0.68 per Intelligence Index task, versus roughly $0.44 for GLM-5.2, despite the identical API token prices.
The difference underscores an important caveat in headline API pricing: Artificial Analysis found GLM-5.3 more verbose than its predecessor, so flat per-token rates do not necessarily mean flat costs for a completed workload.
For developers, though, the immediate change is straightforward: GLM-5.3 is now callable through Z.ai’s API at the same $1.40/$4.40 per-million-token rate as GLM-5.2, giving teams another relatively low-cost option for testing frontier-class coding and agent workloads.

ai.title: WiseTech Raided by Australia Antitrust Watchdog; Stock Sinks
ai.description: WiseTech Global Ltd. said Australian antitrust authorities demanded the company hand over documents and data as part of an investigation into alleged breaches of competition law. The company’s stock tumbled.

ai.title: Motif Technologies CEO on Business Strategy, AI
ai.description: Junghwan Lim, CEO of Korean AI startup Motif Technologies, discusses the company’s business strategy as it works to develop AI models capable of competing with leading global frontier models. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Paul Allen from the AI Summit & Expo in Seoul. (Source: Bloomberg)

ai.title: Funding $1 Trillion AI Capex May Expand Bond Supply, Robeco Says
ai.description: A roughly $1 trillion wave of capital spending tied to artificial intelligence could add to bond supply and keep fixed-income markets volatile as hyperscalers race to fund infrastructure, according to the head of fixed income for Asia at Robeco.

ai.title: Pixel Watch 1 not losing Google Health sleep, workout support
ai.description: On Tuesday, Pixel Watch 1 owners encountered a Google Health error message about needing to update their wearable. Google has confirmed that this was a bug and that the original device remains supported.

ai.title: Bitcoin holds $64,000 and solana leads gains amid 7% Korean chip stock slide
ai.description: Bitcoin held near $64,000 and every major except BNB gained, while Korean semiconductor stocks fell more than 7% and Fed minutes are due at 2 p.m. ET.

ev_autonomous.title: Alphabet to Sell Long Aussie Bond With Record Yield Near 7%
ev_autonomous.description: Alphabet Inc. is poised to pay just under 7% to borrow longer-dated funds in its debut Australian dollar bond deal, in potentially its highest-ever coupon, underscoring how broader demands for cash among hyperscalers around the world are feeding into more costly funding almost everywhere.

business.title: Robot maker Unitree’s IPO surges 600%, outpacing crypto traders’ premarket bets
business.description: A Hyperliquid perp priced Unitree far above its IPO valuation before Shanghai trading began, but the robot maker’s first public trade still opened roughly 75% above crypto traders’ implied price.

business.title: AI Startup Temporal in Talks for a Valuation of at Least $12 Billion
business.description: Temporal Technologies Inc. is in talks for a fresh funding round that would give the AI startup a valuation of at least $12 billion before the new money, according to people familiar with the efforts.
